transcript.text:
High in the Greyhorns, where the cold comes early and the seams of iron and silver run deep, Greyhollow clings to the mountainside like soot to a chimney. Its people live by pick and bellows, and they give their prayers to the Anvil Father, whose temple watches over the town's gates and its dead. Brakka Ironvein has kept those temple doors as a guard for six years, long enough to know every miner's face and the name of every working tunnel.

This afternoon he stands before the one entrance the town stopped naming aloud: the old north workings, sealed a generation ago. Three days ago three miners went down anyway, and none came back. Last night a fourth man crawled out alone, babbling about lights that walk, and died before dawn. At sunrise tomorrow the council means to seal the entrance for good, missing miners or not, so Prior Hessa has asked Brakka to go down before then and bring back whoever can still be brought back.

The mine mouth is a black arch cut into the rock, a cold draught breathing out of it. The borrowed hooded lantern hangs unlit in his hand; behind him the sun is sliding toward the peaks. What does Brakka do?
